_how_it_is_used: server_scripts/grindless/opv/antimatter.js makes one recipe per entry, id grindless:<type>/<name>, with its programmed circuit; 'site' true locks the recipe to grindless:cygnus_x1_orbit; 'wear' inputs are consumed by their chance (out of 10000); 'chanceOut' outputs are made by their chance; 'generator' true writes the EUt negative (a generator type). antihydrogen_synthesis and annihilation_power are package OpV-B3's machine types (data key = dataKey, the EMI line). Package OpV-B3, docs/eras/opv.md machines 3 and 5-8 and process lines 26-28 and 30-33.

recipes._why: machine 3 c1: four cold antiproton cells and four dense positron cells meet in the octupole trap and make four trapped antihydrogen (5% lost to annihilation in the trap: gamma heat in the shield casing). The octupole magnet wears 1/64 a run; 90% of the emptied Penning traps come back
recipes.name: trap_antihydrogen

recipes._why: machine 3 c2: Lyman-alpha laser cooling of the trapped atoms; the laser wears 1/128 a run, 5% of the atoms are lost
recipes.name: laser_cool

recipes._why: machine 3 c3: the cooled atoms are frozen into ice in four levitation trap cells (5% lost). The engine returns the empty cells
recipes.name: freeze_ice

recipes._why: machine 5 c1: one antihydrogen ice cell annihilates against 1,000 mB of hydrogen: 2^29 EU/t for 1,200 t. The gamma absorber tile wears 1/16 a run and comes out activated; 95% of the emptied levitation cells come back. Half of the energy leaves as neutrinos (stated in the tooltip)
recipes.name: burn_ice

recipes._why: machine 5 c2: an ACMF pellet is fired and a stack of antiprotons annihilates in its fireball: 2^30 EU/t for 1,200 t. The tile wears as in c1; the spent hohlraum goes back to the actinide partitioning plant
recipes.name: burn_pellet
